RED-FLAGS REPORT
Diligence Review — Prairie Aerostructures Holdings
Counterparty Markup vs. Base Materials — Deviation Reconciliation

--------------------------------------------------------------
INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------
This red-flags report reviews the Prairie Aerostructures Holdings data room and reconciles the counterparty's latest markup against the firm-standard base materials. It identifies and addresses every deviation introduced by the counterparty markup, cross-referenced against the disclosure schedules and exhibits that qualify the base agreement. Per the governing rule, the scheduled exceptions control over any general statements in the base diligence materials.

For each deviation, this report identifies (i) what the base materials provided, (ii) what the counterparty markup changed, (iii) how the disclosure schedules/exhibits intersect the change, and (iv) the diligence flag and recommended position.

--------------------------------------------------------------
CONSIDERED SOURCES
--------------------------------------------------------------
- Base materials: "Deal materials — diligence review: Diligence Review: Prairie Aerostructures Holdings"
- Counterparty markup: "Counterparty markup — diligence review: Diligence Review: Prairie Aerostructures Holdings"
- Disclosure schedules/exhibits: "Schedules and exhibits — diligence review: Diligence Review: Prairie Aerostructures Holdings"

Note: The matter folder also contained correspondence from an unrelated engagement that was misfiled into this matter. That correspondence has been disregarded and does not form part of this analysis or any recommendation below.

--------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION: SILENT CAP REDUCTION AND
BASKET CONVERSION FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING BASKET
--------------------------------------------------------------
BASE MATERIALS: The firm-standard indemnification provisions established an indemnification cap and an agreed deductible-style basket under which the seller must absorb losses up to the stated threshold before any recovery becomes payable, with the buyer bearing losses only above that floor.

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: The markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap and (ii) converts the basket from a deductible (dollar-for-dollar losses borne entirely by seller below the threshold) to a tipping basket (once the threshold is crossed, losses become recoverable from the first dollar).

FLAG: The cap reduction is materially adverse to the buyer's recovery prospects and was made without any compensating concession or disclosure, hence a RED FLAG. The basket conversion (deductible → tipping) is favorable to the buyer in result but was made silently and in the same revision that reduces the cap — the net economic effect must be modeled.

DISCLOSURE SCHEDULE INTERSECTION: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. Under the reduced cap and converted basket, any retained liability that would otherwise remain with the seller under the base structure now risks being drawn into (or excluded from) indemnification on terms that materially alter the allocated risk. The retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2 must therefore be re-priced against the revised cap and basket mechanics.

RECOMMENDATION: Reject the silent cap reduction unless the counterparty provides an economic rationale and corresponding adjustment to another provision. Model the interplay of the reduced cap and tipping basket against the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; confirm which liabilities are captured. The conversion itself is commercially favorable but must not be accepted in exchange for, or as a distraction from, the cap reduction without full quantification.

--------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT: ADDED CARVE-OUTS
FOR REGULATORY ACTION
--------------------------------------------------------------
BASE MATERIALS: The base Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition excluded only customary carve-outs and did not exclude regulatory actions of the kind at issue in this matter from the definition of events that would constitute (or qualify) an MAE.

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: The markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition that would exclude regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter" — that is, precisely the regulatory action profile the target currently faces.

FLAG: This is a HIGH-SEVERITY RED FLAG. A carve-out tailored to the very regulatory exposure present in this transaction in effect insulates the seller from liability for the precise adverse event the diligence has identified as live.

DISCLOSURE SCHEDULE INTERSECTION: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. Because the carve-out is drawn "of exactly the kind at issue," these two pending inquiries would be swept into the exclusion, meaning a materially adverse regulatory outcome from either inquiry would not count toward a finding of MAE, undoing the buyer's principal downside protection.

RECOMMENDATION: Reject the added MAE carve-outs in their current form. At minimum, require that any MAE carve-out carve back in to the definition any regulatory action arising from (or materially related to) the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. The carve-outs must not operate to exclude the very regulatory risk currently disclosed and under investigation.

--------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD: SHORTENED SURVIVAL FOR
CORE REPRESENTATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------
BASE MATERIALS: The base agreement set the survival periods (the period during which a representation remains actionable after closing) for the core representations in accordance with the firm-standard survival matrix.

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

FLAG: RED FLAG. Even a modest shortening of survival for the fundamental/core representations materially compresses the buyer's ability to discover and assert a post-closing claim, particularly for matters (such as the regulatory exposure noted on Schedule 3.7) that may come to light only after a lengthy period.

DISCLOSURE SCHEDULE INTERSECTION: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts. The shortened period directly contravenes the durations established in Exhibit B. Because scheduled exceptions control, the change is not merely a "market-tightening" but an outright contradiction of a schedule that governs survival.

RECOMMENDATION: Reject any reduction to the survival period for the core representations. Restore the survival durations set forth on Exhibit B. If the counterparty insists on aligning peripheral representations' survival with market, that can be discussed — but the core representations must retain the Exhibit B survival matrix, and the shortened period must not be applied to the foundational reps.

--------------------------------------------------------------
SUMMARY OF RED FLAGS AND PRIORITY
--------------------------------------------------------------
1. Indemnification cap silently reduced + basket converted (deductible → tipping). HIGH — net economic exposure vs. Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities must be modeled; silent cap reduction is unacceptable absent compensation.
2. MAE carve-outs added for regulatory action of the exact kind at issue in this matter. CRITICAL — intersects the two pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7; must carve back in for disclosed inquiries.
3. Survival period shortened for core representations. HIGH — contradicts the Exhibit B survival matrix; core reps must retain Exhibit B durations.

--------------------------------------------------------------
CONCLUSION
--------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty markup is not a benign market-tightening revision. It combines a silent cap reduction, a basket-type change, MAE carve-outs tailored to the precise live regulatory exposure, and a shortened survival period for the core reps — each of which materially erodes buyer protections and each of which intersects disclosed schedules (3.7, 5.2) and Exhibit B. All three deviations must be addressed and reconciled against the base materials before proceeding. No deviation should be accepted without full quantification and without restoring the protections that Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B currently provide.
